Low pressure (cold) liquid ammonia provides refrigeration by removing ambient heat. Removal of ambient heat causes the liquid ammonia (contained within the system) to vaporize. Heat is later removed from the ammonia as it is condensed back into a liquid. Typical operating conditions range from vacuum (approximately 6" Hg) on the low pressure side of the system to 150-160 psig on the high side.
Anhydrous ammonia (CAS #7664-41-7) is used as the refrigerant in the refrigeration process. The total ammonia inventory is above the Threshold Quantity for Accidental Release Prevention.

Executive Summary

RISK MANAGEMENT PLAN AND DATA ELEMENTS

The following subsections outline the Executive Summary requirements of the EPA's 40 CFR Part 68.155.

ACCIDENTAL RELEASE PREVENTION AND EMERGENCY RESPONSE POLICIES

The Vertical Cold Storage, Savannah Pooler facility abides by the emergency action procedures and policies detailed in the Emergency Action Plan manual. 

This Plan was designed to meet the following objectives:
	To prevent loss of life. 
	To minimize and avoid injuries.
	To protect the environment.
	To minimize property damage.

Vertical Cold Storage maintains a safety committee whose members are the designated emergency coordinators for the facility. The Plan provides response organization and notification procedures, evacuation routes, ammonia health hazards, and mitigation procedures which will be implemented to respond effectively to emergency situations that may arise at the facility. This Plan is reviewed and updated at least once per year. This Plan will be reviewed and updated to ensure compliance with the PSM and RMP regulations, as well as to incorporate any facility changes.
STATIONARY SOURCE AND REGULATED SUBSTANCE

1.	On April of 2013 - The site constructed an entire separate process (Engine Room 1) containing an initial charge of 32,500 lbs. of the regulated substances Anhydrous Ammonia.
2.	On April of 2016 - The System was expanding by adding separate process (Engine Room 2) containing 32,500 lbs. of the regulated substances Anhydrous Ammonia.
3.	The combination of both Engine Rooms (ER-1 & ER-2) totals approximately  65,000 lbs. of NH3.

The Vertical Cold Storage, Savannah Pooler facility chills and stores a variety of food products in their cold storage warehouse. FIVE YEAR ACCIDENT HISTORY
There have been no RMP reportable releases of ammonia at this facility over the last five years.
EMERGENCY ACTION PLAN
This Emergency Action Plan addresses procedures for reporting a fire or other emergencies, procedures for emergency evacuation (including type of evacuation and exit route assignments), procedures to account for all employees after evacuation, procedures to be followed by employees performing rescue or medical duties, procedures for handling small chemical releases, and mechanisms to notify external emergency responders when there is aneed for an outside response. Specifically, this Emergency Action Plan addresses the following:
 Emergency Coordination Committees Line of Authority and responsibilities in an
emergency.
 Outlines the process for evacuation of the facility including rally assembly points for
fire and ammonia evacuations.
 Establishes how emergencies are announced and communicated to the warehouse
floor.
 Establishes general procedures for specific types of emergencies.
 Establishes procedures for external notifications and liaisons for official
communication on behalf of the company.
PLANNED CHANGES TO IMPROVE SAFETY
During the Review of the Process Safety Management program at this facility, the Process Hazard Analysis study generated mitigation measures that would improve safety at the Vertical Cold Storage, Savannah Pooler facility located at 220 Nordic Way, Pooler, GA 31322. These action items were entered into ePSM which generates a tracking document that provides reminder communications via e-mails if the recommendation(s) are open past its due date. On an annual basis the technicians at the site complete annual visual inspections of each major piece of equipment. All gaps are documented in ePSM which generates a tracking document that provides reminder communications via e-mails if the recommendation(s) are open past its due da

te.

In addition to the annual visual inspections the site utilizes a third party to perform the 5-year comprehensive Mechanical Integrity Inspection and a Non-Destructive test to determine the condition of the insulation and the quantity of wall loss for selected pipe locations and vessels. The recommendations from this major Inspection are loaded to ePSM which generates a tracking document that provides reminder communications via e-mails if the recommendation(s) are open past its due date.
